note: Round 8 of the Breakdown segmenters (#1241): a fresh real-text sample of 60 (seed 2026102908, rounds 5 to 7's frame) as the headline, a fresh adversarial batch of 10 apart, then the tuning set (round 7's held-out promoted) and the morphemes sets. jev-1.13.0 at 85b3bc8bf, 3 repetitions, the lab's cached jev transport, no reasoning model, no prompt change during the measurement runs. Strict is contractPass; lenient adds the confirmed noun-or-verb tolerance for a compound's first part. The headline leaves out nennen, the one row the two independent judges split on (contested). Intervals: Wilson on attempts, and a case bootstrap of 20,000 resamples with seed 2026102908.
fixes: Outside a verb, a true separable particle that the ADP Case Table lists as a preposition links to its ADP Lexeme, not the verb Prefix (ADR 0054; a19771941): beinahe, überhaupt, zuletzt
When jev weighs a prefixed verb's base a verb of its own, prefix + noun or adjective + citation ending is no longer offered (a19771941): erzählen, verfilmen
Before -ig and -lich, a base that is no adjective but both a verb's stem and a noun is asked between VERB and NOUN alone, the likelier first (a19771941): ruhig, gläubig

verdict: Not yet, but change what is tuned. On the 59 uncontested real-text cases the segmenters are 80.8% exact, strict and lenient (143 of 177; Wilson 74.4% to 85.9%, case bootstrap 70.6% to 90.4%), against round 7's 84.4% and round 6's 89.1% as rescored: the intervals overlap, so no loss is shown, but three fresh samples have not shown a gain either. The round's fixes work where they aim: all three particle words, verfilmen and gläubig pass 3/3, erzählen 2/3, the adversarial batch 29/30, and tuning gains 18 attempts with no case lost. What the fresh sample exposes is structural, not rare-word noise: the form question's headword pick, two suffixes missing from the affix list, and none winning on word + particle adverbs. Fix those three classes in one more round; if the real-text score does not rise, stop tuning these segmenters.
